subject: Clarification: SOC 2 coverage, KMS custody, and subprocessor timelines - BlueCedar
messages:
From: Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@bluecedarhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II, bridge letter and KMS/subprocessor coverage for BlueCedar audit

Hi Tessa / Neha,

We're starting our vendor review for the BlueCedar Health 2026 security audit. Our external auditors (BrightAudit) asked us to confirm a few items about Redwood's SOC 2 Type II coverage and how cloud provider carve-outs / subservice responsibilities map to our control set. Could you please confirm the following by Sep 20 if possible: 

1) Do you have a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the period Jan 1, 2025 - Dec 31, 2025 (PDF)?
2) If any controls are carved out to cloud providers (subservice organizations), can you provide: a) the cloud provider SOC report name and period (e.g., AWS SOC 2 Type II Jan–Dec 2025) and b) a short mapping describing which specific control areas are dependent on those provider reports?
3) For key management: do you use customer-managed keys (CMEK) or Redwood-managed/provider-managed keys for hosted/standard tenants? If provider-managed, can you outline the responsibilities (key custody, rotation, access logging) so we can map to our encryption controls?
4) List of active subprocessors (as of Sep 1, 2026) and whether you have a bridge letter (or subservice carve-out confirmation) for any gaps in audit periods.

Attachments are fine. If a bridge letter is available for a reporting gap (e.g., Q1 2026), that would be helpful; otherwise, a short statement describing compensating controls is OK. Our auditors may follow up with targeted questions.

Thanks — we appreciate a concise export (one-pager + attachments) to attach to our SOC deck. Happy to hop on a 30m call if useful — Sarah (cc'ed) and our auditor will join.

Best,
Sarah Jennings
Senior Information Security Manager
BlueCedar Health

Attachments noted: BlueCedar-RFP-v5.pdf (attached to original request)

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble the materials. Quick confirmation items from our side before we pull the PDFs and bridge material: 

- Which specific encryption controls are your auditors focused on (e.g., data-at-rest KMS custody, key rotation evidence, split-key scenarios for BYOK)? That will help us prioritize artifacts.
- Do you need the full cloud provider SOC report (we can provide vendor report references and redacted vendor PDFs) or a short subservice mapping?

Initial notes: we do have a Redwood SOC 2 Type II report covering Jan 1, 2025 — Dec 31, 2025. For hosted API customers, by default keys are provider-managed (cloud KMS) — we offer a Private deployment option that supports customer-managed keys (BYOK/KMS integrations). I'll ask Marcus (cc) to provide the technical KMS ownership matrix and confirm which hosted services fall inside the subservice boundary.

I'll target a preliminary package (summary + attachments) by Tue Sep 15. If your auditors want a bridge letter for any audit-period gap, please flag which gap they'd like covered (example: Jan–Mar 2026).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-subservice-boundary.csv (stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sarah Jennings <sarah.jennings@bluecedarhealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 13:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II, bridge letter and KMS/subprocessor coverage for BlueCedar audit

Hi all — quick technical summary to help BlueCedar map responsibilities. High-level points: 

- Key management: For our Hosted API (standard customers), Redwood uses cloud-provider-managed KMS keys (default behavior). Redwood manages access controls to those keys via IAM roles and records key usage in audit logs. For Redwood Private customers (VPC/on-prem or dedicated instances), we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) where the customer supplies and controls the key material; Redwood does not retain raw key material in those cases.

- Services in Redwood's subservice boundary: inference runtime, request routing, telemetry and token billing services, object storage for model artifacts and customer metadata. Cloud provider responsibilities generally cover underlying compute, networking, and physical data center controls — which are typically evidenced by the provider's SOC reports.

- Cloud provider coverage: we use AWS and GCP depending on region. Representative reports: AWS SOC 2 Type II (reporting period Jan 1 2025 — Dec 31 2025), GCP SOC 2 Type II (period Apr 1 2025 — Mar 31 2026) for the regions where those providers are primary. We'll include the exact report names and links for the environment your instances are hosted in.

- Subprocessors (live as of 2026-09-01):
  * AWS (infrastructure; SOC 2 report available)
  * Google Cloud Platform (infrastructure; SOC 2 report available for some regions)
  * S3-compatible backup vendor: ArchiveKeep (encryption-at-rest, limited SOC documentation)
  * Telemetry/observability: LogBeat Inc. (subprocessor; SOC report: SOC 2 Type II 2025)

For subprocessors where our contractually-required audit coverage is not co-terminous with your audit window, we can produce a bridge letter or provide compensating control descriptions. I've attached a short KMS responsibility matrix and a CSV that outlines the services in-scope.

- Note on evidence: the full Redwood SOC 2 Type II PDF is available but redacted copy will be supplied first (PII removed). If BrightAudit needs an unredacted copy under an NDA, we can escalate to legal.

Let me know if you want me to call out specific control IDs (CC1, CC2 style) — I can map to BlueCedar's control set tomorrow.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineering Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachment: kms-responsibility-matrix.xlsx (stub)

Tessa / Marcus / Neha — thanks for the quick responses and for the attachments. A few follow-ups from the audit team: 

1) Please provide the Redwood SOC 2 Type II PDF (Jan 1, 2025 — Dec 31, 2025). If you prefer, send a redacted copy first and we'll request the unredacted report under NDA via DocuSign.
2) For the KMS question: we need a concise statement we can attach describing whether key material is customer-controlled (BYOK) for Private customers and that hosted customers default to provider-managed KMS. A one-paragraph statement is fine.
3) For any subprocessors without a SOC 2 report or where the reporting period does not cover Jan–Dec 2025, please provide either: a) a bridge letter, or b) a compensating-controls statement with evidence (logs, contract clauses, encryption config).

Action items from our side: we'll share a DocuSign NDA link for the unredacted report request (we'll send to the Redwood legal contact you specify).

Thanks — our target is to close BlueCedar's vendor evidence package by Sep 30. If you can send the redacted SOC 2 PDF + the short KMS custody paragraph by Sep 16, that will keep things on schedule.

Regards,
A. Chen
Lead Auditor — BrightAudit
